The first World Series, Game 1

Thursday, October 1, 1903, at the Huntington Avenue Baseball Grounds in Boston: the Boston Americans, champions of the new American League, against the Pittsburgh Pirates, champions of the National League, in the first "World's Championship Series." Cy Young pitches for Boston, Deacon Phillippe for Pittsburgh. 16,242 people paid to get in, thousands more than the park could seat, and the overflow stood in the outfield behind ropes.

You arrive on Rogers Street. Buy a ticket at the window, go in through the gate, buy a score card or peanuts, and walk anywhere or sit in any empty seat. Look at a player, the umpires or anything in the park to learn about it. The park, the crowd, the uniforms and the prices are rebuilt from the records of the day; every play of the game will come from the official play-by-play.

WASD walk, drag to look, shift hurry, E buy, sit or stand, V comfort vignette, G skip to the first pitch. In VR: left stick walks, right stick snap-turns, right trigger buys, sits or stands, Y comfort vignette; your money and what you're looking at are on your left wrist, your score card in your right hand.
